newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan copper demand seen flat in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Japan copper demand seen flat in 1996/97.

text.p: Japanese demand for refined copper in the business year ending March 1997 is expected to total 1.49 million tonnes, down 0.6 percent from the previous year, the Ministry of the International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Monday.
"An expected slight increase in copper demand for electric wires is likely to be offset by a decline in output of brass," a ministry official said.
Japan's copper output in 1996/97 is expected to total 1.24 million tonnes, up 1.9 percent from the previous year, MITI said in a revised report.

Operational rates of copper at factories are expected to edge up to 98.1 percent in 1996/97, compared with 97.2 percent last year as smelters increased copper output, backed by a recovery in profitability thanks to higher treatment charges.
The higher charges were supported by the yen's weaker tone as the treatment charges smelters receive from mining companies are denominated in dollars.
